faq.question: What is OppSift?
faq.answer: OppSift is a global opportunity intelligence platform. It brings official tender, grant and commercial notices into one workspace, keeps each notice linked to its issuing source, and helps a team decide what to do next.

faq.question: What types of opportunities can I discover?
faq.answer: Government procurement — tenders, Requests for Quotation, framework agreements and public contracts; grants and funding programmes published by official funders; and commercial Requests for Proposal and supplier opportunities where a buyer publishes machine-readable notices.

faq.question: Which countries are supported?
faq.answer: The market registry, the markets with registered sources and the markets that currently hold collected notices are shown separately in the Markets section. Those counts are read from the platform database rather than from a fixed marketing figure, so a market is never described as covered before it holds records.

faq.question: Where does OppSift obtain its information?
faq.answer: From official publishers: national procurement portals, official search APIs and Open Contracting Data Standard publications. Each stored notice keeps its issuing source, reference number and a link to the original notice.

faq.question: How does eligibility intelligence work?
faq.answer: OppSift separates requirements that are stated in the published notice from facts missing in your organisation profile, and cites the clause behind each confirmed requirement. Eligibility guidance is decision support, not legal advice: the issuing authority's documents always govern.

faq.question: How do I create an account?
faq.answer: Choose Get Started, register with your email address, verify the code sent to that address, then complete the onboarding profile. Email, sector, market and capability details are what make matching and eligibility checks useful.

faq.question: Is OppSift free?
faq.answer: There is a Free plan with core discovery, a baseline organisation profile and a limited number of saved opportunities and alerts. Paid plans add discovery volume, saved records, analysis allowances and seats. New accounts start on Free.

faq.question: How frequently is source information updated?
faq.answer: Each source has a registered refresh interval where one is configured, and every live check is stored with its HTTP result and timestamp. The Markets and Sources sections show the newest recorded check, so freshness is visible rather than asserted.

/.title: OppSift — Global Opportunity Intelligence Platform
/.description: Discover tenders, grants, RFPs and commercial opportunities from official sources in one global intelligence platform. Verified source attribution, market coverage you can check.
/.lead: OppSift brings official tender, grant and commercial notices into one workspace, with the source, the reference number and the deadline kept intact.

sections.heading: Discovery, eligibility and monitoring in one workspace
sections.body: Six integrated capabilities take a notice from discovery to a prepared pursuit: discovery, profile matching, eligibility, opportunity intelligence, monitoring, and preparation with reporting.

sections.heading: Three opportunity categories
sections.body: Government procurement, grants and funding, and commercial Requests for Proposal are normalised into a single record shape with native currency, timezone-aware deadlines and issuing authority.

sections.heading: Market coverage stated honestly
sections.body: Registered markets, markets with registered sources and markets holding collected notices are reported separately, with the newest recorded collection time.

sections.heading: Official sources, attributed
sections.body: Notices are read from official portals and published data feeds. The source showcase states which sources are delivering records, which are registered but not delivering, and which are not integrated.

/global-government-tenders.title: Global Government Tenders — Official Procurement Notices | OppSift
/global-government-tenders.description: Search government tenders and public procurement notices from official national portals and APIs. Compare markets, categories, reference numbers and deadlines in one workspace.
/global-government-tenders.h1: Global government tenders, from the official portals
/global-government-tenders.lead: OppSift reads public procurement notices from national portals, official search APIs and Open Contracting Data Standard publications, and keeps each notice tied to the authority that published it.

sections.heading: What is in a tender record
sections.body: Issuing authority, reference number, procedure type, category, published and closing dates, native currency, disclosed value and a link to the original notice. Missing fields are shown as missing rather than estimated.

sections.heading: Markets with procurement sources
sections.body: Coverage is reported from the platform registry: markets with operational procurement sources, markets whose sources answered their latest live check, and markets that already hold collected notices.

sections.heading: From notice to decision
sections.body: Search by category, market, value and deadline, then compare published requirements against your organisation profile. Confirmed criteria are cited; unknown facts are listed as gaps.

sections.heading: What OppSift does not do
sections.body: OppSift does not submit bids on your behalf and does not replace the issuing authority's documents. Submission happens on the authority's portal.

/international-grants.title: International Grants and Funding Opportunities | OppSift
/international-grants.description: Find international grants, research funding calls and development programmes published by official funders, with award ranges, eligible beneficiaries and closing dates.
/international-grants.h1: International grants and funding, from official funders
/international-grants.lead: Grant and funding notices are collected from official funders and published programmes, keeping the funder, programme, eligible beneficiaries and closing date with the source record.

sections.heading: Funding notices, not funding guesses
sections.body: Where a funder publishes an award range or an eligibility statement, OppSift keeps it. Where a funder does not publish an amount, the record says the value is not disclosed.

sections.heading: Who the funding is for
sections.body: Beneficiary types, eligible countries and consortium requirements are recorded where the notice states them, so a research institute and a small supplier do not see the same call described the same way.

sections.heading: Research, development and non-repayable funding
sections.body: The grants category covers public funding programmes, research calls, development finance and non-repayable grants published by official funders.

sections.heading: Check the call before you commit
sections.body: OppSift links every record to the funder's own page. Programme rules, eligibility and deadlines on the funder's site always take precedence.

/official-data-sources.title: Official Data Sources — Verified Procurement and Funding Feeds | OppSift
/official-data-sources.description: See which official procurement and funding sources OppSift reads, how each is accessed, and whether it is delivering records or only registered.
/official-data-sources.h1: The official sources behind every notice
/official-data-sources.lead: OppSift's credibility rests on where its records come from. This page lists the source ecosystem and states, per source, whether it is delivering records, registered but not delivering, or not integrated.

sections.heading: How a source is counted
sections.body: A source is only counted as connected when it is registered as operational, its latest live check answered, and a successful retrieval is recorded. A registration alone is never presented as a working integration.

sections.heading: What a live check records
sections.body: Each check stores the endpoint requested, its HTTP status, latency, content type and timestamp. A feed that returns an HTML page is recorded as a web page rather than as a working data feed.

sections.heading: Access methods
sections.body: Official search APIs, structured feeds, Open Contracting Data Standard publications and permitted portal monitoring are recorded per source, together with any attribution requirement.

sections.heading: Attribution and licensing
sections.body: Attribution requirements are stored with the source. Where a publisher requires attribution, it travels with the record and appears beside the notice.

/commercial-rfp-opportunities.title: Commercial RFP and Supplier Opportunities | OppSift
/commercial-rfp-opportunities.description: Track commercial Requests for Proposal, supplier registration and subcontracting notices alongside public procurement in one opportunity workspace.
/commercial-rfp-opportunities.h1: Commercial RFPs, in the same workspace as public tenders
/commercial-rfp-opportunities.lead: Corporate buyers publish supplier opportunities in many formats. OppSift treats machine-readable commercial notices with the same provenance rules as public procurement, and says plainly when a source is not machine-readable.

sections.heading: One record shape
sections.body: Buyer, reference, category, value, currency, deadline and source link are normalised so a commercial RFP can be compared with a public tender without re-reading both.

sections.heading: Subcontracting and supplier registration
sections.body: Supplier registration windows and subcontracting notices are recorded where the buyer publishes them openly.

sections.heading: Honest coverage
sections.body: Commercial coverage depends on what buyers publish. Where a buyer only publishes behind a login, OppSift does not claim to read it.

sections.heading: Prepare the pursuit
sections.body: Move a commercial opportunity into the same pipeline as a public tender: tasks, deadlines, documents and internal notes.

/about.title: About OppSift — Global Opportunity Intelligence
/about.description: OppSift is a global-first opportunity intelligence platform built around official sources, explicit provenance and market coverage that can be verified.
/about.lead: OppSift exists because opportunity research is still done by reading dozens of national portals, in different languages, currencies and procurement procedures.

sections.heading: Why OppSift exists
sections.body: A capable supplier should not lose a contract because the notice was published in a portal it does not read. OppSift normalises official notices into one comparable record.

sections.heading: Provenance over volume
sections.body: Every record keeps its issuing source, reference number and a link to the original notice. A record without a verifiable source is not presented as verified.

sections.heading: Coverage without inflation
sections.body: A market in the registry, a market with registered sources and a market holding collected notices are three different claims. OppSift reports them separately.

sections.heading: Neutrality
sections.body: OppSift is not affiliated with any procuring authority, funder or bidder, and does not accept payment to rank a notice.

/contact.title: Contact OppSift
/contact.description: Contact the OppSift team about platform access, source coverage, partnerships or data questions.
/contact.lead: Questions about access, coverage, a source we should be reading, or a data issue in a record: tell us which market and source you are looking at.

sections.heading: Access and plans
sections.body: Ask about team access, plan suitability and paid seats while online checkout is being completed.

sections.heading: Coverage requests
sections.body: Tell us the market, the issuing authority and the portal URL. Coverage requests are reviewed against source access and terms.

sections.heading: Data corrections
sections.body: If a stored record disagrees with the official notice, send the reference number and the source link so the record can be checked.

/docs.title: OppSift Documentation
/docs.description: How OppSift records are structured: source attribution, currency and timezone handling, search operators, and the eligibility boundary.
/docs.lead: How OppSift represents a notice, what its fields mean, and where the platform's interpretation stops.

sections.heading: Record structure
sections.body: A notice record carries its issuing source, reference number, category, publication and closing dates, native currency, disclosed value and canonical source URL.

sections.heading: Dates, currencies and timezones
sections.body: Deadlines are stored with the market's timezone where the source states it. Values are kept in the source currency and are never converted into an invented figure.

sections.heading: Search
sections.body: Search supports keyword, exact phrase, market, region, category, issuer, value range, publication window and deadline window.

sections.heading: Eligibility boundary
sections.body: Eligibility output distinguishes confirmed requirements, missing profile facts and interpretation. It is decision support, not legal advice.

/getting-started.title: Getting Started with OppSift
/getting-started.description: Create an OppSift account, verify your email, complete your organisation profile, and run your first market search.
/getting-started.lead: Four steps from an empty account to a monitored set of opportunities.

sections.heading: 1. Create your account
sections.body: Register with an email address and verify the code sent to it.

sections.heading: 2. Complete the organisation profile
sections.body: Sectors, services, certifications and target markets are what matching and eligibility checks compare against.

sections.heading: 3. Search a market
sections.body: Start with one market and one category, then widen. Save the search once it returns what you want to monitor.

sections.heading: 4. Set a watch
sections.body: Turn the saved search into a deadline and amendment watch so changes reach you instead of being re-checked by hand.

/security.title: Security and Data Provenance — OppSift
/security.description: How OppSift handles authentication, tenant isolation, source provenance and the boundary between public marketing content and workspace records.
/security.lead: What OppSift protects, how it separates public content from workspace records, and how provenance is preserved.

sections.heading: Authentication
sections.body: Accounts use managed authentication with email verification. Sessions are required for workspace routes.

sections.heading: Tenant isolation
sections.body: Organisation data is isolated with database row-level security; workspace records are scoped to the authenticated user's organisation.

sections.heading: Public and private content
sections.body: The public website publishes platform information, market coverage and source status. Opportunity dossiers, saved searches and pursuit records are workspace content.

sections.heading: Provenance
sections.body: Each stored notice keeps the source that published it and a link to the original notice, so a record can be checked against the publisher.

sections.heading: Responsible disclosure
sections.body: Report a suspected security issue to the contact address on the contact page; include reproduction steps and do not test against other customers' data.

/legal/privacy.title: Privacy Policy — OppSift
/legal/privacy.description: How OppSift collects, uses and protects personal data, and the rights available to account holders.
/legal/privacy.lead: This policy explains what OppSift collects, why, and what you can ask us to do with it.

sections.heading: Data we collect
sections.body: Account details you provide, organisation profile information, workspace activity needed to operate the product, and technical logs.

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: To authenticate you, operate your workspace, provide matching and monitoring, and maintain service security.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: Access, correction, export and deletion requests can be made from the account settings or by contacting the team.

/legal/terms.title: Terms of Service — OppSift
/legal/terms.description: The terms that govern use of the OppSift platform, including acceptable use and the status of source data.
/legal/terms.lead: These terms govern access to and use of OppSift.

sections.heading: Use of the service
sections.body: Access is granted to the account holder and organisation named on the account, subject to these terms and applicable plan limits.

sections.heading: Source data
sections.body: Opportunity records are derived from official publishers. The publisher's own documents and portal govern any procurement or funding process.

sections.heading: No bid submission
sections.body: OppSift does not submit bids or applications and does not act as your agent with any authority.

/legal/cookies.title: Cookies and Storage — OppSift
/legal/cookies.description: The cookies and browser storage OppSift uses for sessions, interface preferences and diagnostics.
/legal/cookies.lead: OppSift keeps its browser storage minimal and explains each category.

sections.heading: Essential
sections.body: Session storage required to keep you signed in and to protect requests against cross-site abuse.

sections.heading: Preferences
sections.body: Interface preferences such as theme and language are stored locally in your browser.

sections.heading: Diagnostics
sections.body: Technical logs used to detect failures. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies are set by the public website.

/legal/dpa.title: Data Processing Agreement — OppSift
/legal/dpa.description: How OppSift processes customer data as a processor, including sub-processors, isolation and erasure.
/legal/dpa.lead: Where OppSift processes personal data on behalf of a customer organisation, this agreement describes the arrangement.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.body: The customer organisation is the controller of its workspace data; OppSift acts as processor for that data.

sections.heading: Sub-processors
sections.body: Hosting, database and authentication providers are used to operate the service. A current list is available on request.

sections.heading: Isolation and erasure
sections.body: Organisation data is isolated at the database level, and workspace data can be exported or deleted on request.

/status.title: System Status — OppSift
/status.description: Observed service status for the OppSift web application, authentication, search and billing.
/status.lead: Status is built from what this deployment can observe. A service without a monitoring probe is reported as unverified rather than given an invented uptime figure.

sections.heading: How status is determined
sections.body: The status board reports the web application, authentication, search, ingestion, notifications, AI intelligence and billing separately, with the observation time.
